title: Emergency node stabilization & GPU cartridge swap — runbook (draft)
content:
Status: draft — quick iteration doc for on-call/first responders.

Overview:
This runbook captures a pragmatic path for stabilizing a degraded compute node group (GPU issues, thermal/fabric errors, or sudden pod OOMs) that requires an emergency cordon/drain and, where necessary, a physical or field-repair "GPU cartridge" replacement. The term "cartridge" is used internally for the replaceable GPU sled / accelerator module in our rack units.

Scope:
- Applies to single-node failures causing JVM/worker crashes, sustained GPU ECC/fabric errors, or kernel-level faults that cannot be mitigated via driver restart.
- Includes steps for: detection, triage, safe cordon+drain, swap prep, cartridge replacement, capacity backfill, validation, and rollback.
- NOT for planned maintenance or firmware-wide upgrades. Those follow the standard maintenance playbook.

Assumptions / prerequisites:
- You have SRE on-call Slack access and ability to escalate to HW on-call (rack/hardware team).
- Node has documented serial/rack id and assigned cartridge part numbers in inventory (UCS/asset DB).
- Access to runbook scripts in infra-scripts repo and to the Grafana dashboards.
- An alternate capacity pool (ephemeral backfill) exists for short bursts (label: pool=bridge-ephemeral).

Detection and initial triage (0–10m) — what the first responder should do:
1) Observe alert: typical alerts -> high pod restart rate per node, GPU ECC errors (metric: gpu.ecc.errors > 100/min), worker ping failures, or scheduler backpressure.
2) Check the multi-panel Grafana (GPU health, pod density, queue latency) and the cluster events (kubectl get events -n redwood --sort-by=.lastTimestamp).
3) Run quick diagnostics:
   - kubectl describe node <node-name> | egrep -i "(NotReady|MemoryPressure|DiskPressure|NetworkUnavailable)"
   - kubectl top node <node-name> && kubectl top pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node-name>
   - ssh root@<node-host> sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 400 | tail -n 200 ; sudo dmesg | tail -n 200
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR | egrep -v "driver/library"  # look for ECC, Xid codes, GPU reset attempts
4) Decide: transient vs degraded hardware. If only process-level (OOM/killed) -> follow pod remediation. If GPU ECC / Xid or kernel panics present -> proceed with stabilization path below.

Stabilization path (cordon + drain) — safe mode to avoid cascading failures (10–30m):
- Goal: stop scheduling new pods to the node and gracefully drain existing inference workers without exceeding tail latency SLOs.
- Command set (keep copy in slack/snippets):
  1. kubectl annotate node <node-name> redwood/sre-stabilizing="true" --overwrite
  2. kubectl cordon <node-name>
  3. Use drain with delete-local-data and grace period tuned:
     kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=20m || true
  4. If pods are stuck (eviction blocking because PDBs), escalate to product-owner for permission to force-delete critical pods: kubectl delete pod <pod> -n <ns> --grace-period=30 --force
- Notes: avoid bulk draining of nodes from the same AZ simultaneously. If system-level autoscaler will replace pods slower than expected, spin up ephemeral bridge nodes (see capacity add below).

Cartridge replacement prep (hardware coordination) — non-blocking tasks (15–45m):
- Create incident channel and add HW on-call: #sre-hw + ping @hw-oncall. Post brief: node id, rack/u location, symptoms, recent alert IDs, and customer-impact summary.
- Pull asset record: assetDB lookup for node serial and cartridge SKU. Verify spare availability in the rack/shop. If none, request expedited courier (SLA depends on contract).
- Prepare the node for physical maintenance: ensure node is cordoned/drained and power state known. Note BMC/IPMI access: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc-host> -U admin -P **** sensor | egrep -i "temp|fan|power"
- Create a temporary maintenance ticket in Jira (linked artifact SRE-8421).

Physical swap steps (field tech / rack operator) — checklist to hand off (explicit, copy to hw runbook):
1) Verify identity of server (rack, U position, serial) and confirm spare cartridge SKU.
2) Power down node gracefully if required (if hot-swap not supported): ssh root@<bmc>; ipmitool chassis power soft; confirm OS is down.
3) Follow vendor blade swap procedure: remove sled latch, extract cartridge, inspect connectors for debris/corrosion.
4) Insert replacement cartridge, secure latch, re-seat power connectors.
5) Power on via IPMI: ipmitool chassis power on; watch BMC logs for POST errors.
6) After boot, validate GPU presence: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,uuid,driver_version --format=csv
7) If driver mismatch occurs, run driver bootstrap script: /opt/infra-scripts/gpu/driver-bootstrap.sh && reboot if prompted.
8) Notify SRE via incident channel when node reaches Ready state.

Capacity backfill (add capacity) — temporary steps to keep SLOs (parallel with swap):
- If draining > 5m and tail latency / queue sizes rise above thresholds, bring ephemeral nodes up in pool=bridge-ephemeral. Use terraform/scale scripts: ./infra-scripts/scale/bridge-scale.sh --count 3 --type p4d-ephemeral || runbook: TF apply module=bridge-ephemeral count=3
- Add taint so only inference workloads land: kubectl label node <new-node> pool=bridge-ephemeral && kubectl taint nodes <new-node> dedicated=bridge:NoSchedule
- Monitor autoscaler: check cluster-autoscaler logs and pending pod counts.

Validation (post-swap) — ensure safe return to service (10–30m):
1) Wait until node becomes Ready: kubectl get nodes | grep <node-name>
2) Confirm GPU health: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC ; check no persistent Xid errors in dmesg
3) Run a smoke inference request against pinned test model (internal run): curl -s -X POST https://internal-api/healthcheck -d '{"model":"test-latency"}' - measure p50/p99.
4) Check per-route latency graphs in Console (route: /v1/generate) for reduction of queue.
5) Remove cordon: kubectl annotate node <node-name> redwood/sre-stabilizing-removed="$(whoami) $(date -Iseconds)" && kubectl uncordon <node-name>
6) If immediate spikes or abnormal error rates, cordon again and escalate.

Rollback criteria / abort conditions:
- If node reboots repeatedly (>= 3 reboots in 30m) after replacement, pull node from rotation and tag for deeper HW investigation (ticket to hw-team, key: HW-ESCALATE).
- If driver install corrupts container runtimes or kernel modules, revert to snapshot AMI or golden image using repo tag: ami-rollback:<image-id>.
- If bridge-ephemeral capacity cannot keep latency within SLO for > 30m, failover traffic to fallback-region according to routing policy (contact network ops).

Post-incident actions (to do within 24–72 hours):
- Fill incident timeline in Jira (SRE-8421) with timestamps for: alert, cordon, drain, swap start, swap complete, uncordon, customer impact.
- Attach logs: kubelet journal, nvidia-smi output, BMC dump, dmesg, and Grafana panels.
- Run a retrospective: 30-minute async notes on what worked / didn't; if spare stocking or labeling were the bottleneck, create inventory request.
- Update this runbook with any new heuristics (Xid codes we saw and mapping to 'replace vs soft-fix').

Quick reference (cheat sheet):
- cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- drain (safe): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=20m
- uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>
- node status: kubectl get nodes <node> -o wide ; kubectl describe node <node>
- check GPU errors: ssh root@<host> 'nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR ; sudo dmesg | egrep -i "Xid|gpu|nvrm"'
- BMC: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U admin -P **** chassis power status

Open questions / TODOs (tracking here):
- Formalize spare cartridge SLA and onboard an additional local spare cache for high-volume regions. (Owner: Jules)
- Add automation: one-click draining + ephemeral-scale in infra-console (ticket: infra-413).
- Map top 5 Xid codes to recommended action in this doc (replace vs soft-reset).

Notes to self (informal):
- During last incident (SRE-7569) we saw repeated Xid 62 leading to kernel GPU reset loop; soft reset bought 12–18 hours but recurring — recommend replace.
- Keep the field tech checklist intentionally prescriptive; we've lost time verifying rack ids in the past.

Appendix — useful commands and logs to collect (copy to incident):
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> -o wide > pods-on-node.txt
- kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous > pod-prev-log.txt
- ssh root@<host> sudo tar -czf /tmp/sys-logs-<node>.tgz /var/log/journal /var/log/kubelet.log /var/log/messages ; scp root@<host>:/tmp/sys-logs-<node>.tgz ./
- BMC dump: ipmitool sel elist > bmc-sel.txt ; ipmitool fru > bmc-fru.txt

If anything here is unclear during an incident, default to preserving customer-facing endpoints (latency > availability). Prioritize traffic preservation and call for escalation early.

End of draft.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-08: draft created by Maya Singh
- 2025-01-22: added capacity backfill steps (Evan)
- 2025-02-02: clarified BMC checks and appended quick commands (Priya)
